purpose: Freeze the complete RegionOcrResult persistence that makes a later zero-OCR selector replay possible. This is what actually underwrites capability 3; complete rejection reasons alone do not.
whyRejectionReasonsAloneAreInsufficient: a rejected span returns from analyzeBrandSpan BEFORE a Candidate object is constructed
its brandClass is therefore never calculated
its geometry and words are never placed on a candidate
scoring and ranking run only over candidates that passed the filter ladder, so a rejected span carries no hypothetical score, ranking or ordering
filter outcomes also change later candidate formation: shouldTrimWholeLineCandidate gates line-window generation, and kept candidates become the seeds for multi-line merges
correctRationaleForCapability3: The acquisition preserves the COMPLETE ordered RegionOcrResult array per case. A separately governed, zero-OCR treatment selector can later replay selection over that frozen pass evidence with exactly one filter changed, reconstructing candidate formation, scoring and ranking as production would have produced them. Capability 3 is expected to be satisfiable because of that replay, not because rejection reasons exist.

persistEveryFieldOfRegionOcrResult.transform: RegionTransform, persisted whole: crop, rotate, scale, originalWidth, originalHeight
persistEveryFieldOfRegionOcrResult.timings: OcrPassTimings, persisted whole: preprocessMs, ocrMs, inverseMappingMs, totalMs
persistEveryFieldOfRegionOcrResult.words: OcrWord[], array order preserved, each with text, rawConfidence, bbox and optional originalGeometry

informalSubsetProhibitedNote: The earlier raw-ocr-contract described an informal subset of these fields. A replay needs the whole type, so every field above is persisted exactly and none is summarised.

arrayOrder.why: Production selects over the pass array in order and groups words in emitted order. A reordered replay would not be the same experiment.

perPass: the record validates against the exact closed RegionOcrResult schema
rawWordCount and discardedWordCount are persisted as produced, never recomputed
a SEMANTIC per-pass fingerprint is computed over the validated record with timings removed
perCase: the emitted pass count equals debug.passes.length
pass order matches debug.passes order exactly
a SEMANTIC fingerprint is computed over the COMPLETE ORDERED pass array with timings removed from each pass
assertions.canonicalization: issue-149-candidate-canonical-v1, the same algorithm used for candidate records

haltCodes.PASS_EVIDENCE_TRUNCATED: emitted pass or word count disagrees with the debug object
haltCodes.PASS_ORDER_MISMATCH: persisted pass order differs from debug.passes order

timingsCorrection.priorDefect: Amendment 3 required a canonical fingerprint over the COMPLETE pass record including timings, while determinism-rules.json required exact fingerprint agreement between the primary and repeat runs. performance.now() timings differ by construction, so that pair guaranteed a nondeterminism verdict on every run.
timingsCorrection.resolution: timings are PERSISTED in full for completeness and covered by the artifact integrity hashes, but are EXCLUDED from every semantic fingerprint and from the determinism equality gate. See determinism-rules.json.

exactPersistedRecordSchema.runMetadataNote: Wall-clock start and end, workflow run ID, artifact ID, artifact expiration and runner/host identity live BESIDE the evidence, in a separate provenance record. On a pass record they are an unexpected key and are rejected, so they can never enter a semantic fingerprint by accident.

nestedShapesValidated.triggerReasons: actual OcrPassTriggerReason values, array order preserved
nestedShapesValidated.transform: exactly { crop:{left,top,width,height}, rotate, scale, originalWidth, originalHeight }, rotate one of 0/90/180/270

perWord.bbox: exactly { x0, y0, x1, y1 }, persisted always
perWord.originalGeometry: persisted ONLY when production emitted it; absence is OMISSION, never null; when present it is exactly { imageIndex, x, y, width, height, imageWidth, imageHeight }
